reason: Musculoskeletal is appropriate for this soft-tissue sarcoma umbrella. EBV association is not universal and does not justify infectious_immune across the group.

Cardiac, gastrointestinal and skeletal malformations are defining components. Tracheoesophageal fistula affects the airway in 11/11. Renal and neurologic features are acknowledged and reasonably omitted under the four-axis cap.

Intellectual disability and blepharophimosis define the syndrome. Contractures occur in 6/14; persistent hair and nail abnormalities support dermatologic involvement, including hypoplastic toenails in 4/11.

Craniosynostosis defines musculoskeletal disease. Neurologic involvement is supported by language delay and intracranial hypertension in 9/26; optic nerve hypoplasia occurs in 1/2 assessed. Small denominators justify medium confidence.
This localized subtype affects skin and nails. Gastrointestinal damage associated with generalized dystrophic epidermolysis bullosa is not established for this subtype.
IGF-I resistance defines endocrine disease. Intellectual disability occurs in 30–79%; skeletal maturation abnormalities occur in 80–99%, with structural chest and finger abnormalities in 30–79%.
The tumour originates in the hypopharynx. The rules explicitly assign the pharynx to pulmonary; broader parent classifications do not require gastrointestinal.

Autoimmune thyroid disease defines the endocrine and immune axes. Gastritis/celiac disease and macrocytic anemia occur in 30–79% as syndrome components, rather than merely diseases whose future risk is increased.

Microtia and anorectal malformations support otologic and gastrointestinal primary axes. Vesicoureteral reflux occurs in 2/5, supporting renal involvement. This subtype lacks evidence for common skeletal involvement.

Neuronal ceroid lipofuscinosis is a metabolic storage disease defined by neurodegeneration. Retinal degeneration with visual loss is common in juvenile CLN6 disease; medium confidence appropriately reflects subtype variability.
